summary:
Decide first, then paint: record which rows and columns contain an original 0, and only afterwards set
cells to 0. Painting while scanning would let new zeros cause blackouts of their own. The records can
live in two small arrays, or, for O(1) extra space, in the grid's own first row and first column.

question.md:
Every pixel that is 0 in the **original** grid blacks out its entire row and entire column. Return the
resulting grid.

- **Only original zeros count.** A pixel that becomes 0 because of a blackout must not trigger another
  blackout; otherwise one zero would wipe out the whole grid.
- **Values can be negative or large,** so there's no spare "special" value to use as a marker except
  0 itself.
- **Size:** up to 300 × 300.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Only **original** zeros cause blackouts; zeros created by the blackout must not spread further.
- A zero in the first row or column, which the O(1)-space method uses as storage.
- A grid with no zeros is unchanged.

think.md:
**The trap.** Painting rows and columns as soon as a zero is found creates new zeros, which then look like dead
pixels and black out everything. So first *find* which rows and columns are dark, then paint.
Dead pixels in rows [1, 2] and columns [1, 3]. **Result:**

**Storing the marks inside the grid.** The flags "row r is dark" and "column c is dark" can live in the grid's
own first column and first row: for an inner zero at `(r, c)`, set `grid[r][0] = 0` and `grid[0][c] = 0`. Those
cells will be painted anyway. The first row and column themselves need two extra booleans, recorded *before* any
marks are written, and they're painted last so their marks are read first.

approaches.title: Paint into a copy for each zero

idea.md: Copy the grid. For every original zero, paint its row and column in the copy. Reading from the original keeps new zeros from spreading.

build: For each original zero, paint its row and column in the copy.

lines.text: The result starts as a copy; the original is only ever read.
Black out the zero's row and column in the copy.

notes.c: Report the row count and each row's length.

complexity.md: **Time O(m · n · (m + n))** in the worst case (many zeros). **Space O(m · n)** for the copy.

steps.text: Original (1, 1) is 0: zero row 1 and column 1 in the copy.
Original (2, 3) is 0: zero row 2 and column 3 in the copy.
Every original zero handled. Zeros we wrote never trigger more blackouts, because we only look at the original.

walk.title: Copy the grid. For each 0 in the original, black out its row and column in the copy.

limits.md: Repaints the same lines for every zero on them, and keeps a whole copy. Recording which lines are dark is enough.

idea.md: Two boolean arrays: `zero_row[r]` and `zero_col[c]`. One pass records them, a second paints every cell whose row or column is flagged.

lines.text: One flag per row and one per column: m + n booleans instead of a full copy.
Every original zero flags its row and its column. No painting yet.
Now paint: a cell goes dark if its row or column was flagged. Flags were decided from the original, so new zeros can't spread.

notes.c: Free the flags; only the column-size array is new.

steps.text: Scan once: rows [1, 2] and columns [1, 3] contain a 0.
Second scan: a cell becomes 0 if its row or its column is marked.

walk.title: Record which rows and which columns contain a 0, then zero every cell in a marked row or column.

limits.md: The flags use O(m + n) memory; the grid's own first row and column can hold them.

approaches.title: Use the first row and column as the flags

idea.md:
1. Remember whether the first row and first column originally contain a zero (`row0`, `col0`).
2. For each zero in the inner grid, mark `grid[r][0]` and `grid[0][c]`.
3. Paint inner cells whose row mark or column mark is 0.
4. Finally paint the first row if `row0`, and the first column if `col0`.

**Why the order matters.** The marks are read in step 3, so the first row and column must not be painted
before then; and `row0`/`col0` must be saved before step 2 overwrites those cells.

build: Save whether the first row/column had zeros.
Mark inner zeros on the edges.
Paint the inner grid from the marks.

lines.text: Record whether the first row and first column contained a zero before they're used as storage.
An inner zero marks its row in column 0 and its column in row 0; those cells would be painted anyway.
Paint every inner cell whose row or column is marked.
Paint the first row and column last, from the saved booleans, so their marks were read first.

notes.c: Only the column-size array is new.

steps.text: First: does row 0 contain a 0 of its own? No. Does column 0? No. Save that, because row 0 and column 0 are about to hold markers.
For each 0 inside (rows ≥ 1, columns ≥ 1), write a 0 into the first cell of its row and its column.
Zero every inner cell whose row marker or column marker is 0.
Finally blank row 0 and/or column 0 if they had their own zeros. (Here neither did.)

walk.title: Use row 0 and column 0 themselves as the markers; two booleans remember whether they had zeros of their own.

takeaways.md:
- **Find first, then modify**, when changes would trigger more changes.
- **O(1)-space flags:** store row/column marks in the grid's first row and column; save their own state first.
- **Pitfall:** painting the first row before reading the marks stored in it.
